body:
DELIVERED (safe terminal-item retention advancement + id-safety) + codex-verified (three rounds). Commits 71e2de1e -> f35807c2 -> 3c3eebd1.
The AC-TXN-5A retention-withholding GATE (wired in pqueue-c21635b9) now has a REAL retention-advancement path to withhold:
- HybridProjectionStore::reap_terminal_items (relational.rs) reclaims durable checkpointed-terminal SQLite rows,
  gated to the armed-monitor (hybrid-async) profile only (non-async hybrid/hybrid-strict/sqlite/inmemory unchanged),
  gated by the composition's retention_may_advance so Hard async-apply debt WITHHOLDS it (compose.rs:1130).
- SAFE: reaps only rows the durable SQLite image shows terminal (at/below the checkpoint high-water); recovery
  rehydrates from the SQLite image + object-log tail replay strictly AFTER the checkpoint, so nothing resurrects.
- Proven end-to-end on the REAL composed hybrid-async backend, asserted on DURABLE state
  (durable_resident_terminal_count): withheld under Hard debt, advances once debt drains below the release band,
  survives reopen (0 resurrected).

ID-RESURRECTION SAFETY (codex R1 in the reap review): reaping durable item rows broke mint-counter recovery
(counters were seeded only from surviving rows -> reaping all + reopen-same-epoch could remint a reaped id).
FIXED with a durable additive pqueue_id_high_water table advanced ATOMICALLY with the reap deletion (same tx) and
restored on recovery INDEPENDENTLY of surviving rows, across the ENTIRE relational family that shares the reap:
HybridProjectionStore, SqliteProjectionStore, SqliteRelational (unified), and SqliteRelationalBackend (monolithic).
QueueCounters::observe is monotonic + epoch-aware (ceiling only raises; stale lower-epoch floor can't corrupt a
fresh tenure); the stored ceiling is monotonic across reap batches. Two no-resurrection tests (hybrid-async +
relational) assert the post-reopen mint is strictly past the greatest reaped id — BOTH verified to FAIL without
the fix.
Codex adversarial review (3 rounds): reap safety, gate integrity, non-async-unchanged, atomicity, recovery-restore,
ceiling monotonicity, and the full-relational-family completeness — all SOUND.

HONEST RESIDUAL (row stays PARTIAL): object-log SEGMENT-OBJECT reclamation is deferred — codex confirmed (and the
subagent empirically verified: wiring a trim made reopen fail with "missing segment") that recovery folds the object
log from genesis to rebuild the request-id idempotency maps, so safe segment trim needs a bounded-recovery redesign
(a durable retention floor honored by the idempotency rebuild) that would otherwise regress the proven AC-TXN-3
replay guarantee. Split to pqueue-b5cc2bc7 (P2).

Verify (independent, 0-failed): cargo test -p pqueue-conformance ac_txn_5a -> 6 passed; composed_relational_reconnect
-> 8 passed (incl. composed_relational_reap_all_does_not_resurrect_ids); full -p pqueue-server -p pqueue-sqlite
-p pqueue-conformance -> 506 passed, 0 failed; fmt clean; clippy -D warnings PASS.

Closing for the delivered safe retention-advancement + id-safety scope; the segment-object reclamation
(bounded-recovery redesign) is tracked in pqueue-b5cc2bc7.
summary: safe terminal-item retention withhold->advance proven + id-resurrection safety across the whole relational family (durable id-high-water); codex-verified 3 rounds; segment-object reclamation split to pqueue-b5cc2bc7 (needs bounded recovery)
